meta_title: Private Limited Company Annual Compliance | ROC Filing
meta_description: Complete annual ROC compliance for private limited companies: AOC-4, MGT-7, DIR-3 KYC, auditor and board formalities in one fixed fee plan.
excerpt: One plan that covers every ROC, tax and board compliance your private limited company needs in a year.
intro: A private limited company has fixed annual duties whether it earns one rupee or one crore: audited accounts, ROC returns, board meetings and income tax filing. Miss them and penalties run per day, and directors risk disqualification.

Eaccountingcart bundles the full annual cycle into one managed plan. You share your bank statements and invoices; we handle the books, audit coordination, ROC forms and reminders so nothing is ever late.
what: Annual compliance includes preparation of financial statements, statutory audit by a CA, the annual general meeting, filing of AOC-4 (financials) within 30 days and MGT-7 or MGT-7A (annual return) within 60 days of the AGM, DIR-3 KYC for every director, maintenance of statutory registers and minutes, and the company's income tax return by the due date.

Companies that missed past filings and need regularisation
Founders who want one team for accounts, audit coordination and ROC work

Investor and Bank Ready

One Team, Full Stack

Fixed Annual Fee

Sales and purchase invoices
Previous year's financial statements and returns

why_us: We run compliance on a dated checklist per company, not memory. Clients get reminders before due dates and proof of filing after, every single year.
faqs: My company had no business this year. Do I still need to file?
Yes. Even a zero revenue company must prepare audited accounts and file AOC-4, MGT-7 and its tax return. Non filing penalties apply regardless of turnover.
What happens if annual returns are not filed for two years?
The ROC can strike off the company and directors can be disqualified for five years. Recovering from that costs far more than compliance ever would.
What is DIR-3 KYC?
Every person holding a DIN must verify their details annually by 30 September. Missing it deactivates the DIN and attracts a 5,000 rupee fee to reactivate.
Can you fix past defaults before taking over?
Yes. We compute late fees, file pending forms and regularise the company first, then move you onto the annual plan so defaults never recur.

Eaccountingcart manages the complete LLP cycle: books, Form 11 in May, Form 8 in October, the income tax return and partner KYC, with reminders well before every date.

The LLP's income tax return follows the standard due dates, and designated partners complete DIR-3 KYC annually.

LLPs approaching audit thresholds
Firms that converted to LLP and are new to MCA filings
LLPs with pending defaults and accumulated late fees

May and October filings tracked and completed without you remembering either.

LLP late filing fees accrue daily without limit; timely filing keeps them at zero.
Audit Threshold Watch

Partner KYC Included

Clean MCA Record

faqs: My LLP did nothing this year. Are filings still due?
Yes. Form 11 and Form 8 are mandatory even for nil activity. A dormant LLP that skips them accumulates daily late fees silently.
When does an LLP need an audit?
When turnover exceeds forty lakh rupees or partner contribution exceeds twenty five lakh rupees. Below both limits, the designated partners self certify Form 8.
What if my LLP has years of pending filings?
We compute the exposure, file the backlog and, where closure makes more sense than revival, advise honestly on striking off instead.
Do LLP partners need DIR-3 KYC?
Yes, every designated partner with a DPIN/DIN must complete KYC annually, or the ID is deactivated with a fee to restore.

name: Director Appointment and Removal

meta_description: Appoint or remove a company director with proper board resolutions, consents and DIR-12 filing. DIN application included where needed.
excerpt: Change your board correctly: consents, resolutions and DIR-12 filed on time, with DIN obtained where needed.
intro: Boards change as businesses grow: co-founders join, investors nominate directors, people move on. Each change is a legal event that must be approved, documented and filed with the ROC within thirty days.
Eaccountingcart manages director changes end to end, from DIN and consent formalities to the board resolution and DIR-12 filing, whether it is a friendly appointment or a difficult exit.
what: Appointing a director requires a DIN, written consent in DIR-2, a board or general meeting approval and filing of DIR-12 within thirty days. Resignation requires the director's notice, board acknowledgment and the same DIR-12 timeline; the director may also file DIR-11 to protect their own record. Removal of an unwilling director follows the special procedure under section 169 with proper notice and hearing.
who: Companies adding co-founders, professionals or investor nominees to the board
Directors resigning who want their exit properly recorded
Companies replacing directors after shareholder changes
Boards removing a non cooperative director lawfully
benefits: Deadline Compliance
DIR-12 within thirty days avoids late fees and keeps the master data correct.
Complete Paper Trail
Consents, notices and resolutions drafted so the change withstands scrutiny.
DIN Handling
New directors without a DIN get it through the appointment filing itself.
Exit Protection
Resigning directors get DIR-11 filed so liability ends on the record, not just in fact.
Dispute Safe Removals
Section 169 removals conducted with the notice and hearing the law demands.
documents: PAN and Aadhaar of the incoming or outgoing director
Photograph and contact details of the new director
Consent to act as director (DIR-2) or resignation letter
Digital signature of the director and an existing director
Board or general meeting resolution details
Company master data and MOA/AOA if roles are special
process: Requirement Review
We confirm the type of change and the correct legal route for it.
Documentation
Consents, notices, resolutions and disclosures are drafted for signature.
DIN and DSC

DIR-12 Filing

Records Update
Statutory registers, bank records and other registrations are updated with the new board.
timeline: 3 to 7 working days for standard changes
fees_note: ROC filing fee based on capital; late filing multiplies it
why_us: Board changes done casually resurface in due diligence years later. Our filings come with the complete minute book entries that make future audits and funding rounds painless.
faqs: Can a company have a director without a DIN?
No. Every director needs a Director Identification Number. First time directors can get it through the appointment filing itself, which we prepare.
I resigned but the company never filed it. Am I still liable?
Your resignation is effective from notice, but the public record matters. You can file DIR-11 yourself with proof of the resignation, and we regularly do this for exiting directors.
What is the minimum number of directors a company must keep?
Two for a private company, three for a public company. If an exit takes you below the minimum, an appointment must happen promptly, ideally simultaneously.
Can we remove a director who refuses to resign?
Yes, shareholders can remove a director under section 169 with special notice and an opportunity to be heard. The procedure is strict, and shortcuts get overturned, so it must be run precisely.

name: Registered Office Change

meta_description: Change your company's registered office within the city, across ROC limits or to another state, with all resolutions, approvals and INC-22 filings handled.

excerpt: Shift your registered office, within the city or across states, with every approval and filing done in sequence.
intro: Your registered office is where the law finds your company: notices, summons and official mail all go there. Moving it involves more than a new rent agreement; the change must be approved and filed, and moves across states need Regional Director approval.
Eaccountingcart handles all four types of office shifts, from a simple same city move to full interstate migration, including the newspaper notices and approvals the bigger moves require.
what: A shift within the same city needs a board resolution and INC-22 within thirty days. Moving to another city within the same ROC requires a special resolution. Crossing into another ROC's jurisdiction within the state adds INC-23 approval, and shifting to another state requires altering the MOA, Regional Director approval, newspaper publication and creditor notices before INC-22 completes the change.
who: Companies moving to bigger premises within the city
Startups shifting from a founder's home address to an office
Businesses relocating operations to another state
Companies consolidating group entities at one address
benefits: Right Procedure for the Move
Each shift type has its own route; using the wrong one gets rejected.
No Missed Notices
A correctly updated address means statutory mail actually reaches you.
RD Approval Managed
Interstate shifts, the hardest category, run on our checklist including publications.
Linked Updates
GST, banks, PAN records and licenses updated after the MCA change.
Clean Master Data
Investors and lenders see a consistent address across records.
documents: Proof of new address: utility bill or property tax receipt
Rent agreement and NOC from the owner, if rented
Board and shareholder resolution details
List of creditors and debenture holders for interstate shifts
Digital signature of a director
Altered MOA for interstate moves
process: Route Determination
We identify which of the four procedures your move requires.
Resolutions and Notices
Board and special resolutions, and creditor or newspaper notices where needed, are prepared.
Regulatory Approval
INC-23 applications to the RD are filed and followed for jurisdictional moves.
INC-22 Filing
The address change is filed with proofs within the deadline.
Downstream Updates
GST, bank, tax and license records are updated to the new address.
timeline: Same city: about a week; interstate: 2 to 3 months
authority: Registrar of Companies and Regional Director (MCA)
fees_note: ROC fees per form; RD application fees for jurisdictional shifts
why_us: Interstate shifts fail on publication and creditor formalities. We have the sequence mapped, so your move does not stall at the Regional Director's desk.
faqs: Can I use a residential address as registered office?
Yes, a home address works with a utility bill and owner NOC. Many startups begin this way and shift later, which is exactly the change we handle.
How fast must INC-22 be filed after moving?
Within thirty days of the change. Late filing attracts additional fees and leaves your legal address wrong in the meantime.
Does changing the registered office change my GST registration?
GST is state wise. A move within the state is an amendment; a move to another state needs a fresh GST registration there, which we plan alongside the ROC process.
Why is shifting to another state so involved?

Because it alters the MOA and affects creditors and the exchequer of two states, the law requires RD approval, publications and objection handling. With disciplined paperwork it is routine, just longer.

intro: Businesses outgrow their names: pivots, rebrands, trademark conflicts or a merger that deserves a fresh identity. A company name change is a defined MCA process, and the new name takes effect only when the fresh certificate of incorporation is issued.

Eaccountingcart checks availability against both the company registry and the trademark register, obtains approval and completes the resolutions and filings, then helps update every registration that carries the old name.
what: The process starts with name reservation through the RUN service, checked against existing companies and trademarks. Shareholders approve the change by special resolution, filed in MGT-14, followed by INC-24 seeking central government approval. The ROC then issues a fresh certificate of incorporation, after which PAN, GST, banks and contracts are updated.
who: Companies rebranding after a pivot or market change
Businesses resolving a trademark conflict in their current name
Acquired companies aligning names with the new group
Companies dropping or adding words to reflect new activities
benefits: Conflict Checked Name
We screen MCA and trademark records so the new name survives scrutiny and use.
Correct Sequence
RUN, MGT-14 and INC-24 filed in order without rejection loops.
Continuity Preserved
The company's identity, assets and contracts continue; only the name changes.
Downstream Updates
PAN, TAN, GST, EPFO, banks and major contracts updated with the new certificate.
Brand Protection
We pair the change with a trademark filing so the new name is actually yours.

fees_note: RUN fee plus ROC filing fees; stamp duty on altered documents where applicable
why_us: A name that clears MCA but infringes a trademark is a lawsuit with a certificate. We clear both registers before you print a single new letterhead.
faqs: Does a name change affect existing contracts and assets?
No. The company remains the same legal entity; contracts, assets and liabilities continue. Practically, counterparties are notified with the new certificate, which we template for you.
Can the ROC reject my proposed name?
Yes, if it is identical or too similar to existing companies or trademarks, or uses restricted words. Our screening step exists precisely to avoid burning attempts.
Do I need a new PAN after renaming?
The PAN number remains but the card and records must be updated with the new name, along with TAN, GST and bank mandates. These follow the fresh certificate.
How long is an approved name reserved?
A RUN approved name is reserved for a limited window, generally sixty days for an existing company's change, so the resolutions and filings must move promptly, which our sequence ensures.

name: Increase Authorised Share Capital
meta_title: Increase Authorised Capital | SH-7 Filing and MOA Amendment
meta_description: Raise your company's authorised share capital with resolutions, MOA alteration and SH-7 filing, done before your funding round or expansion needs it.
excerpt: Expand your capital headroom with the resolutions, MOA amendment and SH-7 filing completed in days.
intro: Authorised capital is the ceiling on shares your company can issue. Funding rounds, bonus issues and ESOP pools all fail at the last step if the ceiling is too low, usually discovered at the worst possible moment.
Eaccountingcart increases your authorised capital cleanly: capital clause amendment, shareholder approval and SH-7 filing with the correct fees and stamp duty, typically within a week.
what: Increasing authorised capital requires authority in the articles, a board meeting to convene shareholders, an ordinary resolution altering the capital clause of the MOA, and filing of SH-7 within thirty days with the prescribed fee and state stamp duty on the increased amount. Only after this can fresh shares be allotted up to the new limit.
who: Startups preparing for an equity funding round
Companies planning bonus issues or ESOP pools
Businesses converting loans into equity
Group companies restructuring capital across entities
benefits: Funding Round Ready
The share headroom exists before the term sheet needs it.
Correct Fee Computation
MCA fees and state stamp duty on the increase are computed exactly.
Fast Turnaround
Standard increases complete within about a week.
AOA Check Included
If your articles lack the power to increase, we amend them in the same exercise.
Allotment Support
We continue into the actual share allotment and PAS-3 filing if you are raising.
documents: Current MOA and AOA
Proposed new authorised capital and share structure
Board and general meeting resolution details
Digital signature of a director
Latest master data of the company
process: Structure Review
We confirm the required capital and check the articles for enabling power.
Resolutions
Board and shareholder meetings are documented with the MOA alteration.
SH-7 Filing
The increase is filed within thirty days with fees and stamp duty.
Master Data Update
The new authorised capital reflects on the MCA portal.

Allotments, bonus issues or ESOP grants proceed on the new headroom.
fees_note: MCA fees plus state stamp duty scale with the increase amount
why_us: We time capital increases with the transaction they serve, round, bonus or conversion, so filings, valuations and allotments land in the right order for both MCA and tax purposes.
faqs: What is the difference between authorised and paid up capital?
Authorised capital is the maximum you may issue; paid up is what shareholders have actually subscribed and paid. Paid up can never exceed authorised, which is why increases precede fundraises.
How much authorised capital should a startup keep?
Enough for the next round plus ESOPs, without overpaying fees and stamp duty on headroom you will not use soon. We model this against your funding plan.
Is shareholder approval always needed?
Yes, an ordinary resolution in a general meeting is required, and the articles must permit the increase. If they do not, an articles amendment is passed alongside.
Does increasing authorised capital dilute existing shareholders?
No. Dilution happens only when new shares are actually allotted. The increase itself just raises the ceiling.

name: Share Transfer
meta_title: Share Transfer Procedure | SH-4, Stamp Duty and Board Approval
meta_description: Transfer company shares with valuation, SH-4 execution, correct stamp duty and board approval, documented to survive tax and diligence scrutiny.
excerpt: Move shareholding correctly: valuation, SH-4, stamp duty and board approval with a complete paper trail.
intro: Share transfers change who owns the company, and both the Companies Act and the Income Tax Act watch them closely. Transfers below fair value trigger tax in the buyer's hands, and private companies must respect their articles' restrictions.

Eaccountingcart executes transfers end to end: valuation where needed, SH-4 execution with correct stamp duty, board approval and register updates, with the capital gains position computed before you sign.
what: Shares transfer through form SH-4, executed by transferor and transferee, stamped at the prescribed rate on consideration or fair value, and delivered to the company within sixty days. The board approves and registers the transfer, updating the register of members. Private company articles typically contain pre emption rights that must be followed, and tax rules under sections 50CA and 56(2)(x) police transfers below fair market value.
who: Founders reorganising equity between themselves or family
Investors exiting to incoming buyers
Companies onboarding new partners through purchase rather than fresh issue
Groups moving shareholding between entities
benefits: Tax Safe Pricing
Fair value is determined so neither side faces deemed income surprises.
Articles Compliance
Pre emption and transfer restrictions in the AOA are followed, keeping the transfer valid.
Correct Stamping
Stamp duty computed and paid properly, the classic defect in DIY transfers.
Complete Records
SH-4, board minutes and register entries prepared as one consistent set.
Diligence Proof
The trail satisfies future investors and acquirers examining your cap table.
documents: Share certificates of the transferor
PAN of transferor and transferee
Consideration details and payment proof
Valuation report where applicable
Company master data and AOA
Board meeting details for approval
process: Structuring and Valuation
We confirm pricing against fair value and compute the tax impact for both sides.
Articles Check
Pre emption offers and waivers are documented as the AOA requires.
SH-4 Execution
The instrument is executed and stamped correctly.
Board Approval
The transfer is approved, registered and new certificates endorsed or issued.
Records and Reporting
The register of members is updated and the change flows into the next annual return.
timeline: 3 to 7 working days for standard transfers
authority: Companies Act procedure; tax under the Income Tax Act
fees_note: Stamp duty at 0.25 percent (0.015 percent through depository) on consideration or fair value
why_us: As CAs we handle the valuation and capital gains alongside the paperwork, so the transfer that looks fine today does not become a tax demand two years later.
faqs: Can shares be gifted?

Yes, transfers without consideration are possible, but tax rules deem income for the recipient when fair value exceeds fifty thousand rupees, with exemptions for relatives. We structure gifts to use the exemptions correctly.
Why does a private company transfer need board approval?
Private company articles restrict free transferability; the board's registration of the transfer is what makes the transferee a member. Skipping it leaves ownership legally incomplete.
What valuation applies to unlisted shares?

Fair market value under prescribed rules, generally book value based for tax with DCF options in specific contexts. Pricing far from FMV creates tax in one or both hands, which our computation flags in advance.
Is a share transfer reported to the ROC?

Not immediately by a separate form for private companies; it reflects in the next annual return. The company's own registers and the stamped SH-4 are the primary record, which is why they must be perfect.

Eaccountingcart drafts the amendments, passes them through the proper special resolutions and files MGT-14, so your charter matches what the business actually does and what your investors require.

Both need special resolutions filed in MGT-14 within thirty days, with additional approvals for specific changes such as state shifts. Startups adopting investor friendly articles before a funding round
Companies converting between private and public forms
Businesses cleaning up outdated template charters

Investment Ready Articles
SHA terms mirrored in the AOA are enforceable; loose ends are not.
ROC Clean Drafting
Amendments drafted in registry accepted language avoid resubmission cycles.

why_us: We read your shareholder agreement, licenses and business plans before touching the charter, so the amendment solves the real problem instead of creating three new ones.
faqs: What happens if we operate outside our object clause?
Such acts are ultra vires, beyond the company's legal capacity, creating risk in contracts, banking and tax. Amending objects before starting a new line is quick insurance.
Can the AOA override the Companies Act?
No. Articles operate within the Act; conflicting clauses are void. Our drafting keeps investor terms enforceable within what the law permits.
Do investors really check the AOA?
Always. Diligence compares the SHA with the articles, and unmirrored rights are treated as unenforceable. Adopting restated articles at closing is standard, and we prepare them.
Is shareholder approval needed for every amendment?
Charter amendments need special resolutions, seventy five percent of votes. Board approval alone is never sufficient for MOA or AOA changes.

name: Company Strike Off
meta_title: Company Strike Off | Close a Company with STK-2 Filing
meta_description: Close your defunct company properly through STK-2 strike off: dues cleared, accounts prepared, affidavits and filing handled to end compliance forever.
excerpt: Shut a defunct company the right way, so filings, penalties and director risk actually end.
intro: A company you have stopped using does not stop costing: annual filings stay due, late fees grow and directors remain exposed. Strike off under section 248 is the clean, economical way to close a company that never took off or has wound down.

Eaccountingcart prepares the closure: dues and bank accounts settled, the statement of accounts drawn up, affidavits and indemnities executed and STK-2 filed, then tracked until the ROC publishes the dissolution.
what: Voluntary strike off applies to companies that have not commenced business or have been inactive for two preceding financial years, with no assets, liabilities or pending litigation. The company files STK-2 with a statement of accounts not older than thirty days, director affidavits, indemnity bonds and a special resolution. The ROC publishes the application and, absent objections, strikes the company off the register.
who: Companies incorporated for a venture that never started
Businesses that have ceased operations and cleared their affairs
Group entities being consolidated or simplified
Founders facing growing late fees on a dormant company
benefits: Compliance Ends
No more annual filings, audits or late fee accumulation after dissolution.
Director Risk Closed
Properly closed companies stop threatening DIN status and future ventures.
Cheaper Than Winding Up
Strike off costs a fraction of formal liquidation for eligible companies.
Objection Proof Filing
Pre closure checks with tax and other authorities prevent derailing objections.
Certainty
You receive the ROC's publication confirming the company is dissolved.
documents: Statement of accounts certified by a CA, not older than 30 days
Affidavits and indemnity bonds from all directors
Special resolution or consent of 75 percent shareholders
PAN and bank closure proof of the company
Latest filed financials and returns
Digital signature of a director
process: Eligibility Check
We verify inactivity, assets, liabilities and litigation status against the strike off conditions.
Clean Up
Bank accounts are closed, dues settled and pending filings regularised where required.
Documentation
The statement of accounts, affidavits and indemnities are prepared and executed.
STK-2 Filing
The application is filed with fees and tracked through ROC publication.
Dissolution
The strike off notice is published and the company stands dissolved.
fees_note: Government fee of 10,000 rupees for STK-2 plus documentation costs
why_us: Strike off applications bounce on unfiled returns and unclosed bank accounts. Our pre filing clean up is why our closures go through the first time.
faqs: Can a company with pending ROC filings apply for strike off?
Overdue annual filings generally must be completed up to the end of the year the company stopped activity. We compute the cheapest compliant path before filing STK-2.
What happens to remaining assets or liabilities?
The company must have none at application. Assets are disposed of and liabilities settled first; hiding them is dangerous because directors' indemnities make them personally answerable.
Can a struck off company be revived?
Yes, the NCLT can restore a company within prescribed periods on application by aggrieved parties. That cuts both ways: creditors can also seek restoration, which is why a clean closure matters.
Is strike off the same as winding up?
No. Winding up is a longer liquidation process for companies with assets, debts or disputes. Strike off is the summary route for clean, defunct companies, and we advise which applies to yours.

fees_note: Government fee for Form 24 plus documentation costs
why_us: The expensive question in LLP closure is which pending filings are truly required. We compute that precisely, saving clients from over filing years of forms they never needed.
faqs: My LLP never did any business. Is closure simpler?
Yes. Never commenced LLPs have the cleanest route, often with fewer pending filings. The one year inactivity condition and nil statement still apply.
Do all partners need to sign?
Yes, affidavits and consents from all partners are required. Where a partner is unreachable, the approach must be planned carefully, and we advise on the options.
What if the LLP has a small bank balance or asset?
Assets must be disposed of and the accounts closed before applying; the statement must show nil. We sequence this clean up as part of the engagement.
Can the income tax department object to the closure?
Pending demands or returns can cause objections, so we settle the tax position first. That pre check is the difference between a smooth strike off and a stalled one.

intro: Secretarial audit examines what financial audit does not: whether the board, filings, registers and approvals behind your numbers actually comply with corporate law. For larger companies it is mandatory; for growing ones it is how you find problems before a regulator or investor does.
Eaccountingcart conducts secretarial audits and voluntary compliance reviews in coordination with practising company secretaries, delivering law wise findings you can act on, not a checklist dump.
what: Secretarial audit under section 204 applies to listed companies, public companies with paid up capital of fifty crore rupees or more or turnover of two hundred fifty crore rupees or more, and companies with outstanding borrowings of one hundred crore rupees or more. A practising company secretary issues the MR-3 report annexed to the board's report, covering the Companies Act, securities laws, FEMA and other applicable laws.

Private companies preparing for funding, acquisition or listing

why_us: Our audits end in fixes, not just findings. The CA and CS combination means the same team that spots a gap can regularise the filing behind it.
faqs: Is secretarial audit only for listed companies?
No. Large unlisted public companies crossing the capital, turnover or borrowing thresholds are covered too, and private companies increasingly commission voluntary reviews before fundraises.
How is it different from statutory audit?

Statutory audit opines on financial statements; secretarial audit examines legal and procedural compliance, meetings, filings, approvals, registers. Together they cover both the numbers and the process behind them.
What happens if the report notes qualifications?
The board must explain each qualification in its report. Better practice is remediating what can be fixed during the audit itself, which our process is built around.
We are a private company raising funds. Do we need this?
Not by statute, but a voluntary secretarial review before diligence consistently saves deals from last minute compliance shocks and price renegotiations.
